top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on one clean idea, the magic-wavelength trap that cancels the lattice light shift, followed by careful control of blackbody, collisional and lattice systematics to about 10^-18. That level has been reproduced and surpassed in independent laboratories and cross-laboratory comparisons agree, which is the independent confirmation I require. Credit to Katori (proposal, first demonstration) and Ye (accuracy, many-body regime) is the cleanest on the shortlist, and the citation is scoped to the lattice clock so it is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. Residual concerns are priority of Lemonde, Takamoto and others and the invention-versus-discovery question, but they do not outweigh the award; no award is therefore ranked below it.
